questions.question: Define density, hardness and stiffness, give an example material for each, and explain why stiffness is not the same as strength.
questions.expected_answer: Density is mass per unit volume, for example concrete about 2 400 and steel about 7 800 kilograms per cubic metre, and it decides the dead load of the slab. Hardness is resistance to scratching, denting and wear, for example hardened steel or glass, needed at step nosings. Stiffness is resistance to bending or stretching under load, for example steel and concrete, deciding how much a step or rail flexes. Stiffness differs from strength because a material can be strong but not stiff, like a rubber band, or stiff but not strong, like a biscuit; strength is the load at which it breaks, stiffness how much it deflects below that.

questions.question: Distinguish between flexibility, brittleness and toughness, and use them to justify the choice of concrete reinforced with steel mesh for the ramp slab.
questions.expected_answer: Flexibility is bending without breaking and returning to shape, as in rubber. Brittleness is sudden breaking with little deformation, as in glass, cast iron and plain concrete. Toughness is absorbing energy from a blow by deforming before breaking, as in mild steel and timber. Concrete is dense, stiff and hard enough for a walking surface but brittle, so it would crack under impact and tension; tough steel mesh placed near the tension face holds cracks tight and carries the tension, and slightly rounded nosings reduce chipping, giving a slab with the stiffness and hardness of concrete and the toughness of steel.

questions.question: Explain what rusting is, what speeds it, and compare painting and galvanising as methods of prevention, adding two design measures that reduce corrosion of the handrail.
questions.expected_answer: Rusting is the chemical reaction of iron with oxygen and water to form iron oxide, which is weaker, takes up more space and continues while air and water reach fresh metal; salt in coastal air speeds it. Painting forms a barrier that is cheap and colourful but is scratched and cracked, and rust starts at every break, so it needs renewing every few years. Galvanising bonds a zinc coat by dipping in molten zinc; zinc corrodes in preference to steel, so even scratched areas stay protected for twenty years or more without maintenance, at higher initial cost. Design measures: cap open tube ends so rain cannot collect inside, shape and position rails and post bases so water drains away rather than pooling, and keep steel out of contact with dissimilar metals such as copper.
